analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) UK Data, 2) BRL Update, 3) US Data Centre Production, 4) NVDA Preview and 5) 5 Key Charts 17 Nov 2026
key_insights: UK unemployment fell to 4.6% in September, in line with GS's forecast and a tenth below consensus. GS had flagged that a cohort with a high unemployment rate was dropping out of the sample.
UK October vacancies fell to 690k after September was revised up to 697k. Small business vacancies continue to trend down.
UK flash payrolls for October showed a 34k contraction against consensus for a 10k increase. September was revised up and August revised lower.
UK private sector regular pay growth edged up to 3.1% from 3.0%, in line with expectations. September month-on-month pay growth was softer at +0.13%.

GS expects UK headline CPI to rise to 3.7% from 3.5% and core to rise to 2.9%. Drivers are firmer core goods prices, volatile services components, higher road fuel prices, the Ofgem price cap increase and higher tobacco duties.

Alberto Ramos (GS Latam Economics) says the Brazilian fiscal package sent to Congress failed to impress the market because the measures were mostly short-term and skewed toward raising revenue. His three focus areas are the new Finance Minister, the multi-year fiscal strategy and the new central bank directors.

GS Macro Sales Brazil reports that several large macro funds have closed Brazil FX, rates and equity positions, some keeping only received real rates. Equities lost over R$700bn in market cap and foreigners remain net sellers on the futures exchange.

GS Macro Sales Brazil's outlook is more cautious: Brazil looks cheap but risks being a value trap. A re-rating needs external help (weaker dollar, lower oil) plus credible appointments. Central Bank board nominations are described as an increasingly bigger risk.

GS Brazil rates trading favours front-end receivers up to Jan28, real-rate receivers in NTN-Bs in the 2028-2030 sector, and DI steepeners. The case is a high bar for the BCB to resume hikes in a slowing economy with sticky inflation.

GS BRL FX trading sees too much uncertainty for a carry trade over the next month. It cites a long-USD global bias, year-end seasonality favouring USD with outflows historically past $15bn, and doubts about the fiscal adjustment. It has traded USDBRL tactically by buying dips.

GS Latam Equities Trading says EWZ is down 23% since the election while EEM and ACWI are mostly flat. About a US$1.5bn overhang remains to be sold, redemptions run about US$150mn a day, and desk expects a cleaner position by mid-December.
Bovespa volumes have fallen to US$5bn a day from US$15bn at the election peak, which narrows the exit for money that came in.

On the US midterms and data centres, Geoffrey Okamoto expects no dramatic interruption to data centre building. The new Texas Governor plans to pause new data centre permits until safeguards are legislated, and some hyperscalers have begun agreeing to safeguard terms.

Michael Ng views data centre moratoriums as a temporary pause. He sees added cost as marginal against build cost, so the risk is to timing rather than capacity coming online, and says hyperscaler and tenant demand is very strong.
Jim Schneider expects solid Nvidia 3Q results and 4Q guidance above the Street on better margins. GS 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates are both 6% above the Street.

Schneider sees three debates for Nvidia: management visibility into datacentre power and shell capacity through 2028, sustainability of AI infrastructure funding, and broader AI demand health including agentic CPU upside, customer ROI and enterprise adoption.

Rich Privorotsky says near-term Nvidia numbers could be robust, but the market has no idea what multiple to put on 2028-2030 earnings. Equities are pricing a growth slowdown while rates and FX barely respond. The recent NDX lows are the technical line in the sand: a hold lets a base form, a break risks another mechanical leg lower as CTAs sell.
Sean Johnstone (TMT Specialist Sales) says a minority see downside risk to Nvidia guidance, most see limited near-term risk, and focus is on CEO succession. The bigger debate remains calendar 2028.

Five key charts: GS 12m forecasts show more rates downside, equity upside and selective FX upside vs USD relative to market pricing. GS 2027 policy rate expectations are more dovish than market pricing except in Japan.

GS forecasts gold at $4,650/toz by end-2027 and $5,600/toz by end-2028. GS forecasts France growth of 0.1% next year, well below consensus. A Korea semi sector chart covers 2027 earnings scenarios and potential returns.

market_movers.rationale: GS expects solid 3Q results and 4Q guidance above the Street on better margins, with 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates both 6% above the Street. Results are due after the close on the day of the note.
EWZ is down 23% since the election and about US$1.5bn of pre-election inflows remain to be redeemed at roughly US$150mn a day. The desk expects a cleaner position by mid-December.

earnings_insights: NVDA 3Q results due after the close on 17 Nov 2026. GS 3Q and 4Q EPS estimates are both 6% above the Street (Visible Alpha consensus). GS expects 4Q guidance above the Street on better-than-expected margins. These are forecasts, not reported figures.

NVDA debates ahead of the print: datacentre power and shell capacity visibility through 2028, AI infrastructure funding sustainability, and AI demand health including agentic CPU upside and customer ROI. Sales desk notes a minority see downside risk to guidance and focus on CEO succession.

tension_points.bull_case: Brazil looks cheap, and front-end DI receivers and real-rate receivers capture priced hike premium and high real yields given a high bar for BCB hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: Risks being a value trap: the fiscal package was short-term and revenue-skewed, funds have exited, and heterodox central bank nominations would hurt BCB credibility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Heterodox Central Bank board nominations, or a Finance Minister pick and fiscal package that lack credibility.

tension_points.bull_case: If the recent NDX lows hold, a base can form, and near-term Nvidia numbers could be robust.
tension_points.bear_case: Equities are pricing a growth slowdown while rates and FX barely respond, and a break would risk another mechanical leg lower as CTAs sell and volatility rises.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below the recent NDX lows.
